$comment: Canonical catalog of the LagHound SDK SAMPLE services — the reference apps under sdk/<lang>/example that mount endpoint contract v1 (shared/sdk-contract-v1.json) and that the SDK Endpoints page can provision on demand. One row per language: the port the sample listens on when LagHound deploys it, the Dockerfile that builds it, and the SDK package version it reports as `sdk.version` on GET {prefix}/health. Guarded on every side: C# (SdkSampleCatalog — embedded, served by GET /api/projects/{id}/sdk-endpoints/samples; SdkSampleManifestTests re-derives every `sdk_version` from the language's real package manifest and asserts no `port` collides with shared/http-stacks.json or the endpoint's own 8080/8443/8085) and install.sh (--setup-sdk-samples reads the same ports through the deploy config's endpoints[].sdk_samples). `sdk_version` is the ONLY definition of 'the current sample' — outdated is decided by comparing it against the `sdk.version` a running sample reports, never against the repo release version (each SDK versions independently of the five-file sync).
$ports: 8101-8105 deliberately avoids every port the installers already own on a deployed host: networker-endpoint 8080/8443, the reference-API language server 8085, and the proxy stacks in shared/http-stacks.json (nginx 8081/8444, iis 8082/8445, caddy 8091/8454, traefik 8092/8455, haproxy 8093/8456, apache 8094/8457). examples/docker-compose.yml keeps its own 8081-8085 map: that harness runs the samples ALONE on a dev box, where nothing else is listening.
